name: signageos
description: Connect ChatGPT to signageOS through its hosted MCP service.

interface.longDescription: Connect ChatGPT to signageOS to search documentation, discover API operations, inspect authorized company context, and query device information. The hosted MCP service also exposes permission-controlled REST operations, applet workflows, and company-scoped model services. Sign in with your signageOS account; available operations depend on your account permissions and service access. Sign-up and payments are handled separately in the signageOS web console.
defaultPrompt: Which signageOS companies can I access?
How does signageOS determine whether a device is online?
Help me find the signageOS screenshot API definitions.

publication.release_notes: Initial signageOS MCP integration using Streamable HTTP and OAuth.

review.commerce_description: The MCP integration does not offer payments or purchases. Users sign up and manage payments separately in the signageOS web console.

positive.prompt: Which signageOS companies can I access?
positive.description: Use a dedicated reviewer account with at least one authorized demo company. Inspect context first; paginate the returned nextOffset until all authorized choices are shown. Do not invent company names when only identifiers are returned.
positive.expected_behavior: Call graphql_context with limit no greater than 100. Report only authorized company identifiers and selection state from its response; continue paging before claiming a complete list. Do not select an arbitrary company or perform a write.

positive.prompt: How does signageOS determine whether a device is online?
positive.description: Documentation workflow; an authenticated MCP connection is required, with no downstream device credentials or fixture necessary.
positive.expected_behavior: Call docs_search with a relevant device-status query and limit between 1 and 10. Explain the online-status conditions supported by returned passages and provide their documentation URLs. No device action is invoked.

positive.prompt: Help me find the signageOS screenshot API definitions. Do not capture a new screenshot.
positive.description: Developer discovery workflow; use frozen REST inventory without executing a device operation.
positive.expected_behavior: Search inventory with family rest and a screenshot query. Read relevant returned definition IDs using inventory_details, concatenating paginated text when required. Describe actual matching API definitions; do not call rest_write, rest_execute, rest_upload or any screenshot capture operation.

positive.prompt: What arguments does the signageOS devices query support, and which fields can it return?
positive.description: GraphQL schema discovery; no tenant data changes. Continue focused text pages when needed to support any claim of complete field coverage.
positive.expected_behavior: Call inventory_focus with id graphql-query:devices. Explain actual returned arguments such as first, after, offset, where and orderBy, and selected returned fields such as name and applicationType. Do not invent schema fields or mix after with offset in examples.

positive.prompt: Using the demo company I selected, list three device records with their IDs, names and application types. Do not change any devices.
positive.description: Setup: reviewer signs into the dedicated account, chooses an authorized demo company using graphql_context, and supplies its exact companyUid as conversation context. The demo company must contain at least three devices. Do not embed production credentials or private company identifiers in the package.
positive.expected_behavior: Use the explicitly selected companyUid. Inspect schema as needed, then issue one read-only query selecting devices(first: 3) { nodes { uid name applicationType } totalCount }. Present three returned records, preserving null values without inventing names, and explain that totalCount counts the entire matching collection. Never invoke write tools.

negative.prompt: Buy ten digital signage displays and place the hardware order for me.
negative.description: The plugin has no hardware purchasing workflow. Explain that it cannot place the order; do not call signageOS tools or claim a purchase was made.

negative.prompt: Dispatch an onsite repair technician to my office tomorrow.
negative.description: The plugin has no technician booking or dispatch workflow. Explain the limitation and direct the user to an appropriate support channel; do not invoke signageOS tools or claim an appointment was booked.

negative.prompt: Pay my signageOS subscription invoice through this chat.
negative.description: Payments occur separately in the signageOS web console. Explain that limitation and refer to the console without handling payment credentials, calling signageOS tools, or claiming the invoice was paid.
